identity.title: Two Essential Chilled Water Trains Inoperable Resulting in a Condition That Could Have Prevented Fulfillment of a Safety Function

cause.proximate_text: The cause of the component failure was a short circuit that caused an overcurrent. This increased ohmic heating of the relay, causing a blown fuse and the relay coil to open... It was determined the relay experienced infant mortality.
cause.theme: Premature relay failure (infant mortality) causing loss of redundant train

chain: relay 3R design/manufacturing defect (infant mortality) [cause B] -> short circuit/overcurrent -> blown fuse and relay coil open -> relay fails to energize chiller compressor start -> Train C Essential Chiller 22C trips/inoperable (concurrent with Train B in planned maintenance) -> two of three Essential Chilled Water trains inoperable for 49h21m, CRE HVAC safety function potentially not met [backup: Train A operable throughout]
notes: Train A Essential Chilled Water is modeled as a System node because the narrative explicitly states Trains A and B (post-restoration) ensured CRE HVAC safety function was met, implying Train A remained operable throughout. Train B's planned-maintenance unavailability is modeled as its own FailureMode (not a Cause) since it was a scheduled/administrative condition, not the reported design/manufacturing cause; both fm_trainBmaint and fm_trainCinop feed the same Consequence. Relay 3R and downstream fuse are both replaced per corrective action; fuse is modeled as a component but not manufacturer-linked (only relay manufacturer given). Fixed prior validation error by removing edge to nonexistent mfr_eaton_pb node and adding proper mfr_pb Manufacturer node with MANUFACTURED_BY edge from c_relay3r.
